title: Phrasal Verbs II
description: Idiomatic two-word phrasal verbs whose meaning you can't guess from the parts.

words.definition: to care for a child until it is an adult; to start talking about a subject
examples: She was *brought up* by her grandparents.
Don't *bring up* politics at dinner.

words.definition: to do a task, plan or experiment
examples: The scientists *carried out* several experiments.
We must *carry out* the plan carefully.

words.definition: to find or meet something or someone by chance
examples: I *came across* an old photo of my parents.
Have you ever *come across* this word before?
words.note: Not separable: come across it. Also: come across AS = seem (He comes across as shy).

words.definition: to understand or solve something after thinking about it
examples: I can't *figure out* how this machine works.
She finally *figured* it *out*.

words.definition: to recover from an illness or a sad experience
examples: It took him months to *get over* the breakup.
I'm still *getting over* a cold.

words.definition: to finally agree to something after refusing for a time
examples: The kids asked for ice cream until their dad *gave in*.
Don't *give in* to pressure.
words.note: give in TO someone or something.

words.definition: to experience something difficult; to examine something carefully
examples: She *went through* a hard time last year.
Let's *go through* the answers together.

words.definition: to disappoint someone by not doing what they hoped or expected
examples: I promised to help, and I won't *let* you *down*.
The team *let down* their fans.
words.note: Separable: let someone down. Noun: a letdown.

words.definition: to investigate or examine a problem or situation
examples: The police are *looking into* the case.
I'll *look into* the problem and call you back.

words.definition: to invent a story or excuse; to become friends again after a fight
examples: He *made up* an excuse for being late.
They argued, but they *made up* the next day.
words.note: make up WITH someone. Noun: makeup (cosmetics).

words.definition: a polite way of saying that someone died
examples: Her grandfather *passed away* last year.
He *passed away* peacefully at home.

words.definition: to tell someone a fact or show them something they had not noticed
examples: She *pointed out* a mistake in my report.
The guide *pointed out* the old castle.

words.definition: to delay doing something until a later time
examples: Don't *put off* your homework until Sunday night.
The meeting was *put off* until next week.
words.note: put off + -ing. Separable: put it off.

words.definition: to decide that something is not possible or not suitable
examples: The doctor *ruled out* a broken bone.
We can't *rule out* the possibility of rain.

words.definition: to start a journey; to make something start, such as an alarm
examples: We *set off* early to avoid traffic.
The smoke *set off* the fire alarm.

words.definition: to take control of something
examples: A big company *took over* the small shop.
Can you *take over* while I'm on vacation?

words.definition: to start a new hobby or activity; to use an amount of space or time
examples: I *took up* yoga last year.
This sofa *takes up* too much space.

words.definition: to refuse an offer or request; to make a sound or heat lower
examples: She *turned down* the job offer.
Please *turn down* the music.

words.definition: to happen or end in a particular way, often unexpectedly
examples: The test *turned out* to be easy.
It *turned out* that he was right.
words.note: turn out TO BE... / It turned out THAT...

words.definition: to support someone; to make a copy of computer files
examples: My friends *backed* me *up* in the argument.
Always *back up* your files.

words.definition: to end a romantic relationship; to separate into pieces
examples: They *broke up* after three years.
The ice began to *break up*.
words.note: break up WITH someone. Noun: breakup.

words.definition: to cancel a planned event
examples: The game was *called off* because of rain.
They *called off* the wedding.

words.definition: to reduce the amount of something, especially money you spend
examples: We need to *cut back* on sugar.
The company *cut back* its budget.
words.note: cut back ON something. Noun: cutback.

words.definition: to visit someone for a short time, usually without a plan
examples: *Drop by* anytime you're in the neighborhood.
She *dropped by* my office this morning.

words.definition: to break into pieces; to stop working or succeeding
examples: My old shoes are *falling apart*.
Their plan *fell apart* at the last minute.

words.definition: to continue at the same level; to move at the same speed as someone
examples: *Keep up* the good work!
I walked fast, but she couldn't *keep up*.

words.definition: to succeed in doing something difficult
examples: Nobody thought we could win, but we *pulled* it *off*!
She *pulled off* an amazing performance.

words.definition: to solve a problem; to organize things that are messy
examples: Don't worry, we'll *sort out* the problem.
I need to *sort out* my closet.

words.definition: to be very easy to see or notice; to be better than others
examples: Her red coat *stands out* in the crowd.
His essay *stood out* from the rest.

words.definition: to use something until it can't be used; to make someone very tired
examples: I *wore out* my running shoes in six months.
The long trip *wore* me *out*.
